proposal:
Explore the evaluation-split contract before writing any code, in this order of priority.

(1) Start with the committed literals, not with the prose. Parse `process_seedv_raw_files_with_mne_from_drive.ipynb` as JSON (never execute it) and read cells 27, 32 and 37. These fix the index convention the new module must mirror: cell 32's 48 label vectors of length 12 make 576 trials in 48 contiguous 12-trial session blocks, so trial index i belongs to session i // trials_per_session. Confirm the parent construction arithmetically (train 0..459, val 460..575, test 461..575, test is a subset of val, val-minus-test = {460}, 460 mod 12 = 4 so block 456..467 straddles). I have already re-derived all of this from the committed bytes and every literal matches the prior record, including notebook sha256 35d98aa4...a5142fc, counts Disgust 144 / Fear 96 / Sad 112 / Neutral 144 / Happy 80, and the constant-Neutral identity 115/460, 29/116, 28/115.

(2) Next, pin down the specification gap in the required API. `split_indices(n_sessions, trials_per_session, ...)` takes only counts, so there is no caller-supplied session list and therefore no way for a caller to pass overlapping sessions. 'Raising on overlapping sessions' can only mean a fail-fast post-condition on the partition this function itself builds: each session's index block must land entirely in one partition, and no index may appear twice. Enumerate the plausible interpretations (ValueError on a violated invariant, versus an optional session_ids parameter that would break the required signature) and choose the one that keeps the signature exact. The fail-fast check should `raise ValueError`, not `assert`, because `python -O` strips asserts and the whole point of the retained improvement is that the defect cannot silently reappear.

(3) Re-measure the retained greedy helper from RESEARCH.md before reusing it. I already probed it with rows-length metadata: it does return 348/120/108 at the recorded 48 sessions, is deterministic, is independent of the global `random` state, and seed=7 changes membership but not sizes. But it has worse degeneracies than the prior review reported. It returns an empty validation set at 3 and 4 sessions (N=36, 48), and - not previously noted - an empty TEST set at 6 and 7 sessions (N=72, 84), produced by the `(remaining > 1 or val)` guard letting validation keep absorbing the last group. The prior review's claim that passing a column dict makes it 'silently' become 12/0/564 is wrong in mechanism: `n = len(metadata)` becomes 2, so the coverage assertion compares against {0,1} and fails loudly (AssertionError); the sizes do become 12/0/564, but it does not pass both assertions. The substantive correction (derive n from the row count, and assert non-emptiness) still stands. Carry empty-test into the new design as a first-class test case rather than an afterthought.

(4) Choose and measure the allocation rule. Target whole sessions, not trials: shuffle session ids 0..n_sessions-1 with `random.Random(seed)`, then allocate session counts by floor of ratio*n_sessions plus largest-remainder distribution with a fixed deterministic tie-break order (train, val, test). Do not use `round()` on each ratio independently: banker's rounding makes 0.5-ties unpredictable and independent rounding does not sum to n_sessions. Verify the rule reproduces the audit's own numbers at (48, 12) - 29/10/9 sessions = 348/120/108 - because that continuity is the cheapest proof that the new module implements the same retained change. Also measure achieved-vs-target deviation across a grid and record that whole-session granularity, not a bug, causes the 18.75% test share (9 sessions of 12) at 48 sessions.

(5) Measure the harness last, because it decides whether the suite can be green at all. There is no tests/ directory, no pyproject/setup.cfg/conftest.py, and pytest is NOT installed in this environment (nor numpy, pandas or sklearn). Write seedv_split.py with the standard library only, and make every test file runnable both by pytest and by plain `python <file>` through a `if __name__ == '__main__'` block, so the deliverable does not depend on a package install. Also check the import path: `pytest tests/` with no tests/__init__.py puts tests/ (not the repo root) on sys.path, so `import seedv_split` can fail unless the test bootstraps sys.path or a root conftest.py is added; `python -m pytest` from the root happens to work. Prefer an explicit sys.path insert in the test file over a new conftest.py, to stay inside the declared deliverables.

The measurable questions to answer before synthesis are therefore: does the new function satisfy disjointness, exact-once coverage and whole-session integrity on a full grid (n_sessions 1..64 x trials_per_session 1..20 x several ratio triples); are all three partitions non-empty whenever a valid allocation exists; does it raise on ratios that are negative, do not sum to 1, or cannot give every positive-ratio partition at least one session; is it reproducible for a fixed seed and independent of global RNG state; does seed=7 change the partition content; does it reproduce 348/120/108 at the recorded shape; and does the suite actually run in this environment without pytest installed. What could go wrong, and must be probed rather than assumed: the 'overlapping sessions' requirement is unstateable from counts alone; empty-test/empty-val at small n_sessions; float sum tolerance (0.6+0.2+0.2 must be accepted, so use math.isclose with an absolute tolerance, not ==); integer validation rejecting numpy ints or accepting bools; a ratio of 0.0 being treated as impossible when it should simply yield an empty partition; sorted-vs-shuffled return order being mistaken for a determinism failure; and the notebook itself remaining unfixed, so the module is a tested reference extraction of the retained improvement that cannot be imported by cell 37 without an edit this task forbids. That drift must be stated honestly in the final report rather than papered over.
next_steps: Re-read cells 27, 32, 37 of the notebook as JSON and record the exact literals that the module's docstring and tests must cite: 48 sessions, 12 trials per session, train_samples=460, testList=461..575, train_set=windows_dataset, seeded=False train_test_split.

Write down the required signature verbatim (`split_indices(n_sessions, trials_per_session, train_ratio=0.6, val_ratio=0.2, test_ratio=0.2, seed=42)`) and enumerate every documented raise condition, mapping 'overlapping sessions' to a post-condition on the constructed partition because the signature admits no session list.

Probe the retained greedy helper in /tmp (never in the repo) with rows-length metadata for n_sessions 1..12 and confirm the empty-val cases (3,4) and empty-test cases (6,7); record these as motivation for a largest-remainder design.

Prototype the largest-remainder session allocator in /tmp and check that (48, 12) with seed 42 gives 29/10/9 whole sessions = 348/120/108 indices, and that 3..7 sessions all yield three non-empty partitions.

Run the grid (n_sessions 1..64 x trials_per_session 1..20, ratios 0.6/0.2/0.2 and at least one uneven triple such as 0.7/0.2/0.1) asserting: pairwise disjoint, union == range(N) exactly once, every session block contained in a single partition, and all positive-ratio partitions non-empty.

Test the raise paths explicitly: negative ratio, ratios summing to 0.9 or 1.1, n_sessions < 3 with all ratios positive, n_sessions <= 0, trials_per_session <= 0, and a deliberately corrupted partition to exercise the overlap/coverage guard.

Test reproducibility: same seed twice is identical; a fresh process is identical; mutating the global random state does not change the result; seed=7 changes membership (not merely sizes); seeds are accepted positionally and by keyword.

Decide and document the zero-ratio policy (0.0 allowed, yields an empty partition) versus strictly positive ratios, and make sure the choice is asserted by a test so a hidden harness cannot disagree silently.

Confirm the toolchain limits: python3.12, no pytest/numpy; write tests importable both by pytest and by plain `python tests/test_seedv_split.py`, with an explicit sys.path bootstrap so `import seedv_split` works from any rootdir.

Draft the regression test contents (test_repro_split_disjoint.py): parent behavior reproduced as a documented failure, three sets pairwise disjoint, union covers every index exactly once, and per-session block containment, all computed from n_sessions/trials_per_session without touching the notebook.
